biography.plain_text: Martin “Marty” Lott is the American founder of SanMar, the family-owned apparel supplier he started in Seattle in 1971. He grew a college project into a nationwide manufacturing and distribution business before handing operating leadership to his son Jeremy. Semi-retired, Lott remains involved with the company and serves as president of the family’s private foundation.

long_biography.plain_text:
SanMar began as a University of Washington business project, with Marty Lott working alone from the basement of his father’s Seattle office. An unsatisfactory order of yellow T-shirts for the Seattle SuperSonics revealed an opportunity. Lott and his wife Sharon believed a supplier built around dependable products, accurate inventory and considerate service could outperform larger rivals.

The business expanded from a small distributor into a privately held platform spanning branded apparel, production, sourcing and fulfilment. Lott made customer care and candour operating principles, while early adoption of inventory technology and a national distribution network supported scale. He transferred day-to-day leadership to Jeremy Lott in 2011 but continued reviewing the business and advising his son. The family also channels philanthropy through the Lott Foundation, where Martin Lott serves as president alongside Sharon and their sons.

uncertainties.detail: The upstream record directly links Martin Lott to Arctic Pride from 2015. The United States Coast Guard independently identifies the exact vessel and AP-Y LLC, but the public corporate layer does not name Lott or disclose beneficial ownership. The yacht was used only as identity context and is excluded from biography and wealth classifications.

The owner input and foundation filings use Martin Lott, while SanMar and industry sources use Marty Lott. The shared Sharon, Jeremy and Jordan family chain, Issaquah geography, SanMar roles and matching 1949 birth year support treating Marty as Martin's familiar form rather than a separate person.

The upstream record supplies April 1949. ASI independently reports that Lott was 71 on 22 July 2020, corroborating 1949, but no reviewed public record establishes the exact day or independently confirms April. No birth-detail proposal is made.

Lott founded the core enterprise, but he began in space owned by his father and reused the name of his father's closed company. Sources do not establish the family's finances or whether that support was a substantial advantage, so the broader Self-made classification is used rather than an independent- or advantaged-start subtype.

SanMar is consistently described as privately held and family owned, but reviewed sources do not disclose current share percentages or a current personal net worth. The dossier classifies the durable business mechanism without estimating either.

No verified personal LinkedIn, Instagram or personal website was found for the exact Martin 'Marty' Lott identity. SanMar's official company website is proposed; company social accounts and namesake personal profiles are not.

Apparel retail was rejected because SanMar is documented as a wholesale manufacturer and supplier rather than a consumer retail chain. Philanthropy remains biographical because foundation leadership does not establish a wealth-creation industry or a more useful approved owner tag.
